analysis: The PR is documentation-only: it adds one row for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES to the daemon passthrough table (docs/provider/cli-reference.md:1687) and one row to the environment reference (docs/reference/configuration.md:329). No executable code, authorization, attestation, encryption or key-handling logic changes in the supplied evidence. The variable is described as a deadline-admission estimator tuning knob (per-batch decode charging, anchored isolated-prefill rate, newest-observation freshness), default on, with only 0/false/off/no disabling it. It is documented as forwarded to the launchd provider job. Its security surface is local and operator-controlled (ADV-001 already controls their own environment), and it affects scheduling/availability, not data confidentiality, consumer isolation or trust grants. No relevant threat in the model (T-007, T-010, T-029, T-041, TB-003) has its mitigations invalidated by this documentation. I checked the T-041 TTFT oracle concern: the knob affects deadline-admission estimators, not prefix-cache hit/miss behavior, scope derivation or at-rest storage. The cache TTL, scope and HMAC properties are unchanged. Unverified contract: the actual Swift source (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, LaunchAgent.swift passthrough list) was not supplied, so whether the forwarding claim and the semantics match the code, and whether estimator changes could affect admission or timing behavior, cannot be confirmed. This is a documentation-accuracy question, not an observed regression. The unrelated unchanged text in the supplied cli-reference excerpts was not re-reviewed as new behavior.
